choice.psg: ❶ We might not think of ourselves as global citizens yet, but it’s both necessary and possible to do so. ❷ Some people are skeptical about the idea of global citizenship, but for most of human history, people didn’t think of themselves as citizens of nation-states. ❸ After all, for most of human history, nation-states didn’t exist. ❹ The rise of nation-states over the last few centuries has led people to add state citizenship to other identities, such as family, people group, or religion. ❺ Given the connections between people around the world and the common challenges we face, we need to layer global citizenship on to these other identities. ❻ This doesn’t mean that global citizenship replaces these other identities. ❼ There’s not a single story about our identities. ❽ Instead, it’s precisely because we have obligations to our families, those in our community, and those around the world.

choice.ex: ❺ 다른 부서·회사로 옮겨도 곧 이전만큼 환멸을 느낀다고 했으므로 추론 불가(오히려 반대). 나머지 선지의 근거 문장은 아래 선지별 근거 참고. ① 근거 없음(정답) — 부서를 옮기는 대부분의 직업인들은 남아 있는 사람들보다 결국 훨씬 더 만족하게 된다. ② 근거 ❺❼❽ — 사고방식을 바꾸지 않고 고용주만 바꾸는 것은 직업적 불만족을 해결할 가능성이 낮다. ③ 근거 ❶❷ — 많은 불행한 직업인들은 자신의 큰 노력 없이도 상황이 나아지기를 기대한다. ④ 근거 ❹❺ — 비슷한 직함을 찾아보는 것은 사람들에게 진전을 이루고 있다는 느낌을 줄 수 있다. ⑤ 근거 ❽ — 필자는 같은 행동을 반복하면 같은 종류의 결과로 이어질 것이라고 믿는다.
choice.psg: ❶ Among unsatisfied professionals, there’s a repeating theme — the belief that someday (a mysterious day in the future) things will miraculously change and they’ll stumble into the perfect job or career. ❷ At the same time, they (typically) do little to meaningfully alter their current situation. ❸ They don’t like their job, so what do they do? ❹ They head to job boards and search for roles with a similar job title, hoping that the universe will sprinkle a bit of magic on their career if they just hit the refresh button in a different department or company. ❺ Efforts like this make professionals feel like they are doing something, when really they’re just setting themselves up to take a new role and quickly become just as disenchanted as they were before. ❻ It’s like rearranging deck chairs on the Titanic. ❼ You’ve got to completely switch up your approach. ❽ If you keep playing the same game, you’ll win the same prizes.

opt: Sociologists recommend shortening the working day to make modern employees more productive.

Societies around the world have always agreed on the same retirement age.

(= 65세라는 숫자는 자연이 정한 것이 아니라 사회가 만든 기준이다.) 해설: 답을 기대하는 질문이 아니라 수사 의문문 — 뒤 문장 ❽ 'These numbers ~ aren’t dictated by nature ~ but are social creations'가 의도를 밝 혀 줌. ① 65세는 대부분의 사람들의 건강이 나빠지기 시작하는 나이이다. — ❽이 부정한 '인간의 본질적(생물학적) 특성' 함정 ② 사람들이 더 오래 살게 되면서 은퇴 연령을 높여야 한다. — 은퇴 정책에 대한 의견으로 비약 ③ 사람들이 일을 그만두는 나이는 자연법칙이 아니라 우리가 만든 규칙이다. — 정답 ④ 사람들은 원하는 만큼 오래 계속 일하도록 허용되어야 한다. — 소재만 같은 무관한 주장 ⑤ 전 세계 사회는 언제나 같은 은퇴 연령에 합의해 왔다. — ❸(문화마다 다르다)과 반대

order.ex: (단락 구성 ❶❷ / ❸❹ / ❺❻ / ❼❽) · ❸ 'After all'이 ❷ '사람들은 스스로를 국민 국가 시민으로 생각하지 않았다'의 이유를 보충 · ❺ 'these other identities'가 ❹의 family, people group, religion을 받음 · ❼ 'not a single story' → ❽ 'Instead'로 여러 의무를 제시 (❻ 'This'는 ❺의 쌓기 주장)
order.A: After all, for most of human history, nation-states didn’t exist. The rise of nation-states over the last few centuries has led people to add state citizenship to other identities, such as family, people group, or religion.
order.B: We might not think of ourselves as global citizens yet, but it’s both necessary and possible to do so. Some people are skeptical about the idea of global citizenship, but for most of human history, people didn’t think of themselves as citizens of nation-states.
